name: Römermuseum Aguntum
kurzbeschreibung: The Aguntum Museum near Dölsach in East Tyrol unveils Tyrol's only Roman city with extensive open-air excavations, luxury atrium house, and viewing tower.
preis: Adults approx. €9.50, concessions €8.00, children €5.00, family tickets available
oeffnungszeiten: May to October Monday to Saturday 09:30–16:30 (July & August open daily until 17:00)
beschreibung:
Overview

The expansive archaeological park Aguntum in Dölsach near Lienz is the only verified Roman city located within the modern Austrian province of Tyrol. Chartered under Emperor Claudius in the first century AD as Municipium Claudium Aguntum, this ancient metropolis flourished for centuries as a vital administrative, commercial, and trade centre in the Roman alpine province of Noricum. Today, visitors explore an extraordinary open-air excavation park and an award-winning museum that bring Roman daily life, civil engineering, and luxurious lifestyle in the Alps vividly to life for guests of all ages.

Route & Requirements

The tour begins in the modern museum building displaying precious original artifacts: from fine red Terra Sigillata pottery and delicate gold jewelry to antique coins, tools, and early Christian relics. Guests then explore the vast outdoor excavation grounds under the open sky. Notable architectural highlights include the grand atrium townhouse with hypocaust underfloor heating, the massive town gate and defensive walls, and the expansive public thermal baths. An eighteen-meter-high viewing tower affords a marvelous overview of the city plan and surrounding mountains. Pathways in the park are flat gravel tracks; comfortable shoes and sun protection are recommended.

Visit & Arrival

The museum and excavation grounds are open from May to late October: Monday through Saturday from 09:30 to 16:30 (daily opening until 17:00 during July and August). Admission fees are approx. €9.50 for adults and €5.00 for children; Osttirol Card holders enjoy free entry. Public transport: ÖBB trains and regional buses run from Lienz to Dölsach station or the Dölsach Aguntum bus stop, from where a signposted path reaches the entrance in ten minutes. By car, take the Drautal federal road B100 east from Lienz for four kilometers to the dedicated visitor parking area.

Tips

In the on-site cinema, an engaging documentary film provides a vivid recreation of Roman urban life two millennia ago. Children can participate in an archaeological quiz rally with a dedicated dig area. After your visit, head to the nearby Tristacher See lake to conclude your cultural outing with a refreshing swim in idyllic woodland waters. The museum shop offers quality replicas of ancient Roman jewelry.
